passage:
After his night rounds, Harish stayed on in the hospital's biomedical workshop and pulled out the service logbook for the ICU machines. Six entries in March, all signed by Suresh, his senior and friend, who had taught him everything in his first week.
He checked the gate register. Suresh had been on leave on four of those dates.
Maybe someone else signed for him. Maybe the dates were copied wrong. Harish wrote it all down, dates side by side, and went to see Ojas in stores.
'Did we issue filters for the ICU machines in March?'
Ojas scrolled. 'Nothing since January.'
Harish walked back slowly. He thought of Suresh's daughter's wedding card on the workshop wall. Then of the patients on those machines tonight.
He needed to be sure. He wasn't yet.

qa.q: On how many of the six March dates was Suresh on leave?
qa.a: Suresh had been on leave on four of those dates.

qa.q: What conflicting feelings does Harish have as he walks back?
qa.a: He feels loyalty and affection for Suresh, who taught him everything, and worry for the patients on the machines tonight.

qa.q: What is wise about how Harish is handling this stage?
qa.a: He is quietly gathering facts, checking other records and considering innocent explanations, so he is sure it is real before raising it.

qa.q: What might the ICU patients' families be trusting in without knowing it?
qa.a: They are trusting that the machines their relatives depend on have really been serviced.

grounding: It shows an employee quietly checking records, considering innocent explanations and weighing loyalty to a colleague against patients' safety.

passage:
Subject: can you tell me if I'm being paranoid
Hi Lavanya,
You know accounts much better than me, so I need a sanity check. No names, just the shape of it.
At work I process vendor payments. One cleaning supplier gets paid every month, but I've never seen their staff in the building, and our floors are cleaned by the in-house team. I looked up the supplier's address on the invoice. It's the same building as my manager's flat.
I've gone through every invoice for a year and listed them. I asked facilities, casually, who the outside cleaners were. They didn't know of any.
Maybe it's a sub-contract I don't understand. My manager has been kind to me. I don't want to ruin someone over a mistake.
Is there an innocent explanation I'm missing?
Charu

qa.q: Whose flat is in the same building as the supplier's address?
qa.a: The supplier's address is the same building as Charu's manager's flat.

qa.q: What is Charu worried about in asking Lavanya?
qa.a: Charu worries about being wrong and ruining a kind manager over a mistake, while also feeling uneasy that the payments may be fake.

qa.q: What makes Charu's approach sensible at this stage?
qa.a: Charu is gathering facts quietly, checking with facilities and asking an informed friend for innocent explanations before deciding whether to act.

qa.q: How might Lavanya feel receiving this email?
qa.a: Lavanya may feel trusted and a little concerned, wanting to help Charu think it through carefully.

grounding: It shows an employee quietly gathering facts about suspicious payments and asking whether there is an innocent explanation before acting.
